[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: tables are read left to right, top to bottom, as the only natural order, and 'row' and 'column' are easily swapped. Rule: the loop that is outside decides the order: an outer loop over rows i gives row-major order, an outer loop over columns j gives column-major order.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: row-major order processes a 2-D array row by row; column-major order processes it column by column.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: for (i < M) { for (j < N) ... a[i][j] } is row-major; for (j < N) { for (i < M) ... a[i][j] } is column-major. Both keep a[i][j] with i as the row.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing (row-major print): i = 0, j runs over 0..N-1 printing a[0][j], newline; i = 1, ... So a[0][0], a[0][1], ..., a[1][0], ... in that order.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: row-major processing yields per-row results (row averages in column N, rows printed as lines); column-major yields per-column results (column averages in row M).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: each inner step processes one entry; each outer step completes one whole row (row-major) or column (column-major) and resets the per-row sum.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Because a[i] is a row array, row-major order walks along each row array in turn; column-major jumps between row arrays at each step.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Which loop is outside decides whether entries are processed row by row or column by column; the inner loop finishes for each outer value.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: choose the order that matches the result wanted, row-major for per-row results (and for printing), column-major for per-column results.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Conservation: swapping the loops of an element-wise operation (copy, add) keeps the result and changes only the visiting order. For printing or per-row sums, swapping changes the output (transposed layout, column results).
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: use row-major by default in Java (rows are arrays; printing goes line by line). Use column-major when the result is per column, and remember that ragged arrays have no full columns.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Each loop bound must match the index it controls (i < M rows, j < N columns). Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: after swapping the loops the bounds are not swapped with them, so in a non-square array a[i][j] gets i up to N-1 (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Per-row or per-column accumulators must be reset for each outer pass. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: sum is declared before the outer loop, so each row average includes all earlier rows
Which loop is outside decides whether the entries are processed row by row or column by column.
Row-major order visits a[i][j] row by row (outer loop over i); column-major order puts the column loop outside.
